page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard4.Ax.120 is a bare-metal compute server built on the x86_64 architecture. The platform features an Intel Xeon 6987C-P processor operating at up to 3.9 GHz, supplying 120 physical cores and 240 hardware execution threads across dedicated CPU resources. The physical hardware is accompanied by 1152.0 GB of total system memory, providing approximately 4.8 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The server profile does not include integrated local solid-state storage or discrete GPU accelerators, meaning persistent file systems and boot disks depend entirely on remote block volumes or network-attached storage. Connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource footprint presents a balanced ratio between physical execution units and memory capacity, avoiding virtualization hypervisor overhead by delivering direct hardware access.

Without local NVMe drives, operational efficiency relies on scaling I/O via external storage fabrics while dedicating all 240 hardware threads to compute and in-memory operations. BM.Standard4.Ax.120 is suited for large-scale enterprise applications, high-concurrency web serving platforms, large memory-resident caching tiers, batch processing pipelines, and parallel distributed computational tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard4.Ax.120 is a dedicated bare-metal server configured for compute-intensive and balanced enterprise enterprise workloads. Driven by an Intel Xeon 6987C-P x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, it features 120 physical cores and 240 vCPUs alongside 1152.0 GB of system memory. This architecture yields a balanced distribution of 4.8 GB of RAM per thread without hypervisor virtualization layers. The server does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The server is well positioned for large parallel compute jobs, large-scale memory caching, batch data processing, container clustering, and high-throughput application serving.
